summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted following gastrostomy tube removal due to symptomatic hypoglycemia with blood glucose of 35 mg/dL, likely exacerbated by fasting and her history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. She experienced dumping syndrome after oral glucose administration and required IV dextrose and close metabolic monitoring. During her hospitalization, she was advanced from clear liquids to a Stage IV bariatric diet without complications, remained hemodynamically stable, and had no further episodes of hypoglycemia. She was discharged home with instructions on frequent small meals, blood glucose monitoring, wound care, and medication management, including new prescriptions for pantoprazole and promethazine. Follow-up was arranged to monitor for long-term metabolic and gastrointestinal stability.
